correctness.rationale: Six nonnegative ballot multiplicities are uniquely determined by one integer t in a necessary and sufficient closed interval. Direct ballot counting produces three mutually exclusive strict Condorcet conditions. Reversal of a pairwise majority along the integer fiber forces a one-step separation for odd electorates and at least two steps for even; the two cycle decompositions give the sharp bound n>4d. Endpoint residual ballots classify exactly the n=5 and n=10 equality layers. Multinomial ordered-voter counts have an explicitly decreasing adjacent ratio. The standalone exact integer program directly enumerates 8,007 anonymous ballot multisets and 6,291 rank matrices through n=10; finite checks support, rather than substitute for, the general proof.

value.rationale: Identifiability of a strict Condorcet outcome from aggregate rank marginals is a fundamental voting-information question raised by the 2023 paper. This theorem provides all-electorate closed feasibility and exact distribution for the first nontrivial candidate count, proves the sharp parity split in minimum voters for hidden winner disagreement, classifies the complete first odd/even ambiguity layers, and quantifies the resulting conditional uncertainty. These natural first-information-loss thresholds and global feasibility formulas add motivated structure beyond finite known-table recomputation.
